(p-224) Surah al-'Asr

There are two views concerning it.

The first: that it is Makkan. This was stated by Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn al-Zubayr, and the majority.

The second: that it is Madinan. This was stated by Mujahid, Qatadah, and Muqatil.

His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿By the 'Asr﴾. There are three views on this.

The first: that it is time (al-dahr). This was stated by Ibn 'Abbas, Zayd ibn Aslam, al-Farra', and Ibn Qutaybah. He swore by time only because it holds a lesson for the one who reflects, in the passing of night and day according to a measure that never breaks down.

The second: that it is the late afternoon (al-'ashiyy), which is the period between the sun's passing its zenith and its setting. This was stated by al-Hasan and Qatadah.

(p-225) The third: the 'Asr prayer. This was stated by Muqatil.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: This is the answer to the oath.

"Mankind" (al-insan) here means people, as you might say, "The dirham has become abundant in the hands of the people," meaning the dirhams. Khusr and khusran have one meaning. The scholars of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: Khusr is the loss or diminishing of one's capital. So if a person does not employ himself in what brings him lasting profit, he is in loss, because he has worked toward the ruin of himself, and these two are the greatest of his capital. ﴿Except those who believe﴾, that is, those who have affirmed the truth of God and His Messenger and have acted in obedience, ﴿and enjoin one another to the truth﴾, that is, to the oneness of God (tawhid), the Qur'an, and following the Messenger, ﴿and enjoin one another to patience﴾ in obedience to God and in upholding His law. Ibrahim said in his interpretation of this surah: When a human being is granted a long life in this world, he is in decline and weakness, except the believers, for the rewards of the deeds they used to do in their youth and health will continue to be recorded for them.
